seo_title: Cost of Living in Budva 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Budva per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A resort town on the Adriatic with 30 days visa-free entry and a large Russian-speaking community of relocators. Ideal for seaside living with a clear path to a residence permit through property.
pros: The sea, beaches and a Mediterranean climate
30 days visa-free entry plus an easy path to a residence permit through property
A large Russian-speaking community in the resort area
Close to Kotor, Tivat and ferry connections to Italy
cons: Strong seasonality — a tourist boom in summer, empty in winter
Prices are higher than in Podgorica, especially in high season
A weak job market — almost everyone works remotely
Local healthcare is expensive and limited

best_places.name: Budva Old Town
best_places.description: A Venetian fortress on a cliff by the sea — narrow streets, restaurants and boutiques.

best_places.name: Mogren Beach
best_places.description: The most beautiful beach of the Budva Riviera, surrounded by cliffs — 10 minutes from the old town.

best_places.name: Sveti Stefan
best_places.description: A postcard island-hotel 15 minutes from Budva — a symbol of Montenegro.

best_places.name: Konoba Stari Grad
best_places.description: Classic seafood in the old town — fish, squid and Njeguši prosciutto.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 30 days without a visa; extend by leaving to Serbia or Bosnia.

visa_steps.title: Registration (Beli karton)
visa_steps.description: Within 24 hours of moving in — the landlord registers it at the police.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit through property
visa_steps.description: Buying any home grants a 1-year residence permit — the most popular route for Russians.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit through business
visa_steps.description: Opening a DOO (LLC) — a 1-month process, with a 9% corporate profit tax.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: CKB, NLB, Erste — they open accounts for Russians but require a residence permit or proof of residence.

faq.question: How does Budva differ from Podgorica?
faq.answer: Budva is the sea and resort life, Podgorica is the capital and work. Many live in Podgorica and holiday in Budva.

faq.question: What is winter like in Budva?
faq.answer: +8–12°C, few tourists, quiet. Some restaurants and shops close until Easter.

faq.question: Where to live with children in Budva?
faq.answer: Budva, Bečići, Sveti Stefan — there are international kindergartens and one school, Adriatic College.

faq.question: Is it hard to buy property in Budva?
faq.answer: Russians can buy freely; the minimum threshold is from €50,000, and a residence permit is issued automatically.

faq.question: What about banks in Budva?
faq.answer: CKB, NLB, Erste — they work with Russians who hold a residence permit. Without one, opening an account is difficult.

faq.question: Can I work remotely in Budva?
faq.answer: Yes, many freelancers register a DOO — a 9% tax and access to EU routes.

reviews.text: We bought a flat in Bečići with a sea view for €120,000 and got a residence permit. Winters are quiet and overcast, but summer is paradise.
I lived in Podgorica, then we moved to Budva. The sea, the quiet, friends from the relocator community. The downside — high season is exhausting.
